title: BACHELOR TOWN
text:
98 THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE


BACHELOR TOWN

Amid an humble shady grove
    That had lately been cut down,
In all its odd and dreary looks,
    There was a bachelor town.

At sunset, or at evening's close,
    The bachelors might be seen,
In playing marbles, other games,
    Or getting dishes clean.

When night appeared in all its shade,
    When all its inmates there,
Each one was steadily engaged
    To have at least his share.

All supper o'er and things prepared,
    All seemed to be engaged
In poring over classic lore,
    Or ancient history page.

For four long hours or more,
    The busy work went on.
Some still were busy at their books,
    And some to bed had gone.

At break of day, their spirit gay,
    And all was joy in town;
Some busy seated at their books,
    Some getting breakfast found,

To eat their breakfast at such a time,
    According to their rules;
Not very long they might be seen
    All seated in the school,

Their minds were fixed on their abstruse book,
    Nor could it well be said,
By the tutor's voice or classmate's sign,
    Won't you get your lessons, Webb?

With all the force of hero's power,
    They seem to eye their books,
And in the sequel of the class,
    Were cheered by the instructor's looks.

Many useful things they oft would learn
    By the use of each other's aid,
And would calmly return to their quiet home
    When all their lessons were said.³³

³³The Platonian Messenger, op. cit., Vol. I, No. 6, April 20, 1885.
